purpose: Flag InterPro domains whose cross-genome count variation reflects organellar-genome insertions or transposable-element content rather than nuclear protein-coding gene copy-number variation. Flagged domains are RETAINED in the matrix but excluded from variance rankings by default.
organellar_regex: Ribulose bisphosphate|photosystem|Photosystem|plastid|Plastid|chloroplast|Chloroplast|thylakoid|NADH|NAD\(P\)H|Cytochrome b6|cytochrome c oxidase|Cytochrome c oxidase|ATP synthase|ATPase, F|Maturase|maturase|Ycf|CemA|PsbA|RuBisCO|rubisco|Mitochondrial|mitochondrial ribosom|Ribosomal protein.*chloroplast
evidence: On the 26-genome Pfam-only prototype, 6 of the top 15 most CV-variable domains (mean>=5, present in >=20 genomes) were organellar or TE-derived: NADH-quinone oxidoreductase subunit D (IPR001135, cv 0.748), Helitron helicase-like domain (IPR025476, cv 0.565), chloroplast envelope membrane protein CemA (IPR004282, cv 0.547), RuBisCO large subunit C-terminal (IPR000685, cv 0.527), NADH:quinone oxidoreductase/Mrp antiporter membrane subunit (IPR001750, cv 0.519), and ATP synthase alpha subunit C-terminal (IPR000793, cv 0.491). The rank-15 cutoff was cv 0.473. Further flagged domains rank just outside the top 15 (e.g. RuBisCO large subunit ferredoxin-like N-terminal IPR017443 at rank 22, cv 0.425; Photosystem I PsaA/PsaB IPR001280 at rank 30, cv 0.410). These reflect plastid/mitochondrial sequence carried into nuclear annotations and transposon annotation depth, not gene CNV.
completeness_check: CV was verified NOT to be driven by annotation completeness: of the top 40 CV domains, 0 had Pearson r>0.7 with per-genome annotated gene count and 35 had |r|<0.3.
